audits.title: Remote Mentorship Using Video Conferencing as an Effective Tool to Strengthen Laboratory Quality Management in Clinical Laboratories: Lessons From Cambodia.
audits.standard: ISO 15189 laboratory quality management system standard

cycle1.result: Pre-implementation audit scores (figures not given in abstract)

audits.intervention: Laboratory quality management training with in-person and remote video-conference mentorship

cycle2.result: Significant improvement in audit scores across all sections of ISO 15189

audits.other_findings: Improvement correlated with time spent in video-conference mentoring (mean 6,027±2,454 minutes per laboratory); participating laboratories scored higher than non-participating ones.
audits.citation: Donovan G, Ong SK, Song S, Ndefru N, Leang C, Sek S, et al.. Remote Mentorship Using Video Conferencing as an Effective Tool to Strengthen Laboratory Quality Management in Clinical Laboratories: Lessons From Cambodia. Glob Health Sci Pract. 2020;8(4):689-698. doi:10.9745/ghsp-d-20-00128. PMID: 33361236.

audits.title: Enhancing accreditation outcomes for medical laboratories on the Strengthening Laboratory Management Toward Accreditation programme in Kenya via a rapid results initiative.
audits.standard: SLIPTA checklist toward ISO 15189 accreditation (star rating)
audits.setting: 39 medical laboratories on the SLMTA programme
audits.intervention: Rapid results initiative: high-level management stakeholder engagement, needs-based expedited SLIPTA mentorship and on-site support
audits.other_findings: Laboratories had stagnated for 2-7 years before the initiative.

audits.title: Accreditation of a molecular HIV diagnostic laboratory following the Strengthening Laboratory Management Towards Accreditation (SLMTA)-Stepwise Laboratory Quality Improvement Process Towards Accreditation (SLIPTA) approach in Kenya: an implementation science study.
audits.standard: WHO SLIPTA checklist for ISO 15189 compliance across 12 quality system essentials; turnaround time target 80%
audits.setting: KEMRI HIV Laboratory, Alupe, public molecular diagnostic laboratory
audits.intervention: SLMTA approach with targeted mentorship, on-site workshops and training
audits.other_findings: Viral load EQA scores rose from 60% to 90%; accreditation awarded March 2017.

audits.title: 'Fifteen percent of microbiology reports are wrong!': further experience with an internal quality assessment and audit scheme.
audits.standard: Internal quality assessment by specimen resubmission (consistency of results)

cycle1.result: Mean discrepancy rate nearly 15% in the first two years.

audits.intervention: Audit of microbiologists' comments added with a standardised scoring scheme; laboratory techniques altered and staff training (sputum bacteriology, anaerobe recognition, better cabinet lighting).

cycle2.result: Overall discrepancy rate fell from 9.4% to 3.2%; 325 (7.4%) resubmitted specimens gave discrepant results.

audits.other_findings: Staphylococcal and mixed-culture urine recognition and faecal microscopy remained hard to fix; 20.3% discrepancy in medical comments but only 0.4% likely to change outcome.
audits.citation: Farrington M, Amphlett M, Brown DF, Messer S. 'Fifteen percent of microbiology reports are wrong!': further experience with an internal quality assessment and audit scheme. J Hosp Infect. 1995;30 Suppl:364-371. doi:10.1016/0195-6701(95)90040-3. PMID: 7560974.

audits.title: Mind the gap: Improving the performance of the reference laboratory to end-tuberculosis in Armenia.
audits.standard: ISO15189:2012 quality management standard (TB SLMTA assessment checklist)
audits.intervention: Quality management system introduced with twice-yearly assessments.

cycle2.result: Progressed to one star; all laboratory indicators improved except culture positivity in smear-negative TB.

audits.other_findings: Client management and customer service and evaluation and audits stagnated.
audits.citation: Cholakyans V, Kabasakalyan E, Denisiuk O, Akopyan K, Davtyan K, Akhalaia M, et al.. Mind the gap: Improving the performance of the reference laboratory to end-tuberculosis in Armenia. J Infect Dev Ctries. 2019;13(5.1):10S-15S. doi:10.3855/jidc.10935. PMID: 32049660.

audits.title: Implementing laboratory internal audit to improve compliance and quality of care in the municipal public health system-based ambulatory care health clinics in New York city.
audits.standard: New York State Department of Health Clinical Laboratory Evaluation Program, using a modified audit checklist
audits.setting: Laboratories in municipal public health system ambulatory care clinics (Gotham Health NYCHHC), New York City

cycle1.result: First audit conformity documented across operational, quality and compliance metrics (figures not reported separately).

audits.intervention: Formal plan and tailored audit checklist; findings from first audit acted on before re-audit 6 months later.

cycle2.result: Overall 84% increase in compliance and conformity, ranging from 63% to 100% across categories; 0% nonconformity in 75% of sites.

audits.other_findings: Staff shortages, rapid turnover and lack of retraining contributed to sites not reaching 100% conformance.
audits.citation: Huq Ronny FM, Sherpa T, Saquib FN, Ahmad S. Implementing laboratory internal audit to improve compliance and quality of care in the municipal public health system-based ambulatory care health clinics in New York city. Lab Med. 2025;56(2):115-117. doi:10.1093/labmed/lmae088. PMID: 39557406.
